1  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
In this appeal, the petitioner has challenged the judgment dated 31.12.2015 in MVC.No.2797/2013 passed by the MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru (SCCH- 25).

entities.text: MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru
entities.label: JUDGE

sentences.text: 2. The parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. Brief facts of the case are, on 02.04.2013 at about 7.15 a.m. while the petitioner was riding the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA05-HW-4067, hit by the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA50-F-191 at Sampige road, Malleshwaram causing injury.

After taking treatment at Vegas Hospital, Bengaluru,
she approached the Tribunal seeking grant of compensation.
Claim was opposed by the BMTC.
After taking the evidence, the tribunal passed the impugned judgment by awarding compensation of Rs.2,64,030/- with 8% interest.
Urging inadequacy and NC: 2023:KHC:41002 seeking enhancement the petitioner has filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard Sri.Suresh M.Lathur, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the BMTC.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioner that the petitioner has suffered leg injury, a lady aged '38' years, beautician by profession, injury to her leg affected her professional carrier and she cannot persuade the same with same efficiency due to the permanent disablement and the percentage of disability at 8% taken by the tribunal is inadequate contrary to the medical evidence.
The petitioner was earning Rs.22,000/- per month, but the tribunal has assessed the income of Rs.7.000/-, without adding the future prospects and the compensation awarded is meager.

Compensation awarded towards 'loss of amenities' and 'discomfort' is on the lower side,
'loss of income during the laid up period' is only considered for three months instead of six months,
no NC: 2023:KHC:41002 future medical expenses is awarded though evidence is let in through the doctor and sought for enhancement of compensation.

6. Per contra, learned counsel for the BMTC has contended that the petitioner though suffered a injury to the foot, there is no evidence that the said injury has caused any permanent disablement,
petitioner persuade her beautician job by sitting.
He has fairly admitted that in the year 2013, the income may be assessed at Rs.8,000/- but putting a rider.
Future prospectus cannot be added to the income considering the disability on account of the injury.
According to him, a nominal enhancement may be awarded towards 'loss of amenities and discomfort' and it is not a case for awarding future medical expenses and he supported the impugned judgment.

sentences.text: I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments addressed on behalf of both the parties and perused the materials on record.
Material on record did point out that there was an accident involving the motorcycle of the petitioner and the BMTC bus.
Accident took place in the busy road of Malleswaram, Bengaluru.
The petitioner was under hospitalization and she has spent more than Rs.77,000/- towards treatment as per Ex.P.9.
Injury certificate did point out that the petitioner has suffered Bimalleolar fracture of medial malleolus and lateral malleolus.
She underwent ORIF surgery with fixture of 1/3rd tubular plate at the fracture sight.
PW.2/Doctor, whose evidence points out that the petitioner suffered with 25% whole body disability.

PW.2 is not a treating Doctor and having regard to the fracture and the avocation of the petitioner,
it could be taken at 10% whole body disability irrespective of the medical opinion.
As fairly admitted by Sri.F.S.Dabali, learned counsel for the respondent-BMTC that in the year 2013, a person with no proof of income is assessed at Rs.8,000/-.
Though petitioner claims that she is a beautician and also doing Tupperware business, she has not produced any evidence to that effect.
Hence, the NC: 2023:KHC:41002 petitioner is treated as a person with no proof of income, hence her notional income is assessed at Rs.8,000/- for the purpose of calculation.

9. In a case of this nature, the award of compensation shall not be a windfall nor pittance to the petitioner, but at the same time, this Court has to consider that a '30' year old lady doing profession sustained injury on her ankles, it will certainly effect her carrier as a working women.
At the same time, it shall not be penalty for the BMTC to enrich the petitioner and the Court has to award just compensation in the circumstances taking into all consideration.
The argument of BMTC that the future prospects shall not be added is not persuasive.
Future prospects is added taking into consideration the compensation awarded for the 'loss of future income due to disability'.
One cannot dispute that earning person cannot be less then the notional income.
Hence, future prospectus has to be taken into consideration at 40% for the age of the petitioner and multiplier applicable is '15'.
By following all these aspects, compensation has to be assessed.

Towards pain and suffering Rs.40,000/-, loss of amenities and discomfort 40,000/-, medical expenses Rs.77,070/-, loss of income of 4 months at Rs.8,000/- is Rs.32,000/-, attendant and incidental charges of Rs.5,000/-.
As regard 'loss of income due to injury' is concerned, as observed above, 10% whole body disability is taken.

The calculation will be Rs.8000/- + Rs.3,200(40%) =11,200/- x 12 x 15 x 10% = 2,01,600/-
and this will be a 'loss of future of income on account of the injuries'.

Thus the total compensation comes to Rs.3,95,671/- as against Rs.2,64,034/- thereby enhancement of Rs.1,31,637/- rounded of to Rs.1,32,000/- for which the petitioner is entitled and it is the just compensation in the facts and circumstances of the case.

sentences.text: As regards rate of interest is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded 9% interest.

In the year 2013,
no Banks will offer interest at 9%.
There is no uniformity in NC: 2023:KHC:41002 several judgments as regards rate of interest is concerned.
Keeping in mind the prevailing Bank rate of interest, awarding of interest at 6% is reasonable.

In this regard, it is relevant to refer to a decision of the Division Bench of this court in Ms.Joyeeta Bose and Ors. -vs- Venkateshan.V. and Ors. in M.F.A.No.5896/2018 c/w M.F.A.Nos.4444/2018 and 4659/2018 (MV) DD 24.08.2020 with reference to Section 149(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Rule 253 of Karnataka Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Section 34 of Civil Procedure Code, wherein at Para 52 has laid down principles regarding award of interest.

It reads thus:
"52.Thus, under Section 34 of CPC being squarely applicable to the interest awarded by the tribunal and Section 34 empowering the tribunal to award pendente lite interest and discretion being vested with the Court/Tribunal to award interest from the date of suit or petition is to the maximum extent of 6% p.a. or in other words, not exceeding 6% p.a., the contention raised by the learned Advocates appearing for the Insurance Company deserves to be accepted and accordingly, it is accepted.
As seen from the catena of decisions, only in the cases where special reasons are recorded, higher rate NC: 2023:KHC:41002 of interest is awarded.
Here in this case, the Tribunal has not assigned any reason for awarding higher rate of interest.
The interest awarded by the Tribunal at 9% per annum is not comparable to prevailing Bank rate of interest at relevant point of time.

Hence 6%
interest is to be awarded in the facts and circumstances of this case.

13. In view of the above discussions, the appeal merits consideration in the result, the following:
ORDER a) Appeal is allowed-in-part.
b) The impugned judgment and award is  modified.
c) The petitioner is entitled to enhanced  compensation of Rs.1,32,000/- with interest at 6% p.a. for the date of petition till date of deposit.
